correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=2 a comparison odometer (2,1,...,1) has Laplacian image (2m-2)e_u; the first-excess proof bounds actual topplings even with a potentially negative comparison terminal height. A precise Dhar-burning bijection identifies extremal recurrent states with recurrent states of the graph H obtained by deleting the drive; spectral determinants give both counts; stationarity gives the mean; product limits give e^-1. Exhaustive recurrent-height and stabilizer checks for m=2,3,4, exact determinant and Green-system tests for m=2..10, and an independent bijection checker passed.

originality.rationale: Examined primary text on complete-graph/wheel avalanche polynomials and recurrent-state decompositions does not give the antipodal-drive double-toppling formula on cocktail-party graphs. The closest neighboring work treats adjacent-drive, different topology, or recurrence classification without this event. Results are compared by implication; the established one-toppling theorem requires drive adjacency to the sink and therefore cannot imply a two-toppling event at its unique nonneighbor. Searches and accessible previous results did not produce an equivalent or stronger formula; unindexed equivalences remain possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed exact enumeration or a general complete-multipartite avalanche polynomial may imply the claim.
Full text of the complete-bipartite paper and some older avalanche literature was not inspected; no whole-paper absence is inferred from abstracts.

value.rationale: The matched missing edge creates a physically meaningful departure from the adjacent-drive single-toppling regime. Exact maximal-event configurations have a natural spanning-tree bijection and nontrivial product count for all m>=2; despite event probability asymptotic to 1/(2em), maximal events account for a positive asymptotic 1/e fraction of the mean activity. This is structurally motivated and useful for finite driven-dissipative sandpile comparisons, not a routine finite-table recomputation.
